## SETUP (one time)

1. REQUIRED status columns: the current `datasets/tickets-eval-10.csv` already includes blank `s1_status` and `s2_status` Text columns. If your table was imported from the earlier CSV without them, add both TEXT columns by hand (Add Column) - do not re-import and duplicate the tickets. The claim step writes STALE markers before any scoring, and the update node does not auto-create columns: without `s1_status` the run stops before any model call. All other `s1_*` columns are created automatically on first write.
2. Table names must be exact: **Get Run Status**, **Claim Run**, **Mark Rows Stale (S1)** and **Record Progress** look their tables up BY NAME - `tickets eval 10` and `comparison runs`, spelled exactly like that. Nothing to select in those four nodes, and do NOT touch their table pickers: picking a table by hand switches the node off name lookup and can blank its column mapping.
3. Select `tickets eval 10` in the ONE node that still needs a pick (its node type has no by-name mode): **When fetching a dataset row**. **Write Results to Dataset** follows that pick automatically through an expression - do not touch its table field. Pick the `tickets eval 10` table specifically: the name-based nodes resolve that exact table. If `comparison runs` does not exist yet, import `datasets/comparison_runs.csv` as a new table - the importer names it `comparison runs` (header-only on purpose: every column imports as Text, zero rows - the workflows fill it), or create it by hand under that exact name with TEXT columns: `key`, `status`, `batch`, `expected`, `processed`, `started_at`, `completed_at`.
4. Make sure ollaya (port 11435) is running on the host with the `laya:en` model.

## RUN (single operator, one run at a time)

**Execute workflow** on the canvas (full run from the trigger). n8n walks all 10 rows automatically, one execution per row. Each row runs through **System 1 only** (ollaya laya:en) and the `s1_*` columns are written back to the same rows: team, confidence, urgent, computed route, correctness flags against `expected_team` / `expected_urgent` / `expected_route`, two latency numbers, two token counts, and a `s1_run_at` timestamp. Token counts are ollaya's own reported `usage.input_tokens` / `usage.output_tokens`: a 0 is a real measurement (the classifier generates no text), a blank means the backend did not report the count. Input tokens come from a different tokenizer than S2's - compare as reported usage, not identical units of work. The `expected_*` label columns are never written.

**Latency, measured identically on both systems:** `s1_wall_ms` is the client-side wall time around the ollaya call (the same measurer wraps the S2 call in the other workflow - use wall for the headline comparison). `s1_server_ms` is ollaya's own reported total_duration (load + eval), a corroborating server-side number.

**Before trusting the results:** `comparison_runs` key `latest_s1` must show YOUR run from start to finish - it flips to `running` with a fresh `started_at`, and results are current only once it shows `complete` with `processed` = `expected`, and every row's `s1_run_at` is at or after the run's `started_at` - a row with an older timestamp is leftover from a previous run, not part of this one. Anything else (never went `running`, stuck `running`, old timestamps) means the visible results are not from a finished run.

**Recovery:** stop any active execution of this workflow (Executions list), set the `latest_s1` status cell to `aborted`, then rerun.

Run **System 2 Eval** separately to fill the `s2_*` columns on the same 10 rows - same tickets, same expected labels, independently executed.

Fail-closed freshness: when a run claims, every row's s1_status is set to 'STALE since <ts>'; as each row completes it becomes 'current as of <s1_run_at>'. A row still showing STALE holds previous-run s1_* values - never read it as current. An interrupted run therefore leaves visible STALE markers (and comparison_runs stuck 'running' until set to 'aborted'). Residual window: the claim and the stale-marking are one node apart, so a kill exactly between them can leave previous values unmarked - but that failure always leaves the key stuck 'running', blocks later runs, and writes no new results. One operator, one system at a time: run the S1 and S2 workflows sequentially - concurrent runs against the same table have not been verified.

value.s1_status: ={{ 'STALE since ' + $now.toISO() + ' - a new S1 run is in progress; s1_* values on this row are from a previous run' }}
